task.description:
Execute fn:git-merge per docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md for feature/WF03-ISS0200-20260821. Use the NON-worktree variant: this checkout is the PRIMARY entry holding main (re-verify with `git worktree list` rather than taking it on trust). All gates are green -- Step 03 PASS after one rework, Step 03b FAIL then 03c PASS, Step 05 PASS, Step 05b closing gate PASS. rework_count 1 of 3. Queue task 200 is already released `done` and GH#391 is already CLOSED, both verified by ORCH from real output, so this step must not repeat either.

THIS BRANCH IS DOCS-AND-HANDOFFS ONLY. ORCH verified: `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | grep -E '^(lib|test|priv|web|config|mix)'` returns nothing. Verify that yourself before relying on it. Consequence for GIT_MERGE.md step 5d and the PR body's Validation block: the suite's standing failures are cleared by ATTRIBUTION ROUTE 1 -- structurally, this branch cannot have caused any test failure, because no module, test file, config or dependency appears in the diff at all. State that route and that evidence in the PR body per the protocol's explicit warning against a bare verdict. Do NOT write a bare `PASS` next to a non-zero count, and do NOT run the full suite as a ritual: route 1 is satisfied by the diff itself, and `core-directives.md`'s "Failure Attribution Is Structural" is the canonical rule. Run `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` only if the rebase touches anything compilable, which it should not.

⚠️ THE REAL WORK OF THIS STEP IS THE REBASE, AND IT IS NOT ROUTINE. origin/main moved from 7322185 to 9d277ea while this run was in flight -- 15 commits from TWO sibling sessions (WF03-ISS0201-20260821 and WF03-ISS0204-20260821) running in other checkouts. ORCH measured the overlap: three files are touched by both sides.

  1. docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md -- THE DANGEROUS ONE, and the danger is SEMANTIC, not just textual. ISS-0201 applied three wording riders to SECTION 2 -- the same section this run added its measured-negative-result block to -- and ISS-0204 settled the `started_at` question. Read GIT_MERGE.md's SEMANTIC conflicts guidance and apply it: ask, for every passage either side changed, whether the other side also changed its meaning even with no textual marker there. Specifically, ISS-0201's rider 3 concerns the obligation to add a source path to `artifacts_in` when a restatement is dropped, and rider 1 concerns the schema fence's `backfill_note` member -- both live in section 2 alongside our block. Compose both intents; do not pick a side.
     HARD CONSTRAINT that survives the rebase: ISS-0200's AC4 says section 4's validator-re-derivation requirement and section 2's FOUR WORKED EXAMPLES must be byte-identical to what they were. They have now been certified byte-identical three times (03c and 05b hashes: worked examples ab6ccd4def262cac, section 4 cf3e25d6580c07c1, section 4.1 13e1699dc0155a1c, measured against 7322185). A rebase can silently clip a span. RE-VERIFY those hashes AFTER the rebase completes and quote them. If a sibling session legitimately changed those spans, that is not a violation by us -- report it plainly rather than reverting their work, and say so.
     Also re-check after the rebase: the section-2 JSON schema fence must still parse (it is declared machine-loadable), and the 6,000 WARN threshold must still be DECLARED in exactly one place.

  2. handoffs/orchestrator.log and 3. handoffs/registry.json -- both APPEND-ONLY, both written by all three sessions. ORCHESTRATOR.md section 7.1 governs: resolve by UNION, never re-serialise, reorder or overwrite another session's entry, and re-validate that registry.json still parses afterwards. A commit that shrinks orchestrator.log's line count is a defect -- check the line count before and after and quote both. The rebase-conflict flag inversion warning in GIT_MERGE.md step 5b applies: during a rebase `--ours` is main and `--theirs` is your replayed commit, the opposite of merge. Do not use either flag from habit; hand-resolve and then re-read the resulting file before claiming what you kept.

If conflicts exceed GIT_MERGE.md step 5a's threshold, abort and report FAIL rather than forcing. Do NOT force-push under any circumstance.

PR title: "fix: ISS-0200 measured — result.summary carries no redundancy defect; add the `no_defect` status [WF03-ISS0200-20260821]". Body per GIT_MERGE.md step 7, with the SECURITY-REVIEWER line reading "out of scope (docs and handoffs only; no API route, migration, secret, or response-shaping code in the diff)" and a one-line summary of the outcome: the issue was investigated and measured to carry no defect, which is a legitimate resolution its own acceptance criteria declared up front, and the run's product is the recorded measurement plus the vocabulary that lets a no-defect outcome be stated honestly.

Then merge, and do the MANDATORY local cleanup in step 9 -- return to main, pull, delete the branch, and verify all four checks. Report the real outputs.
